# Deferral Ledger

One line per deferral. Never close a task silently with a forward reference —
record what landed, what was deferred, and where to resume.

The `status` column tracks consumption of each deferral by milestone **M0119**
(see `docs/milestones/0119-deferral-ledger-backlog-consumption.md`). Values:
`-` = open / 未対応 (not yet consumed); `resolved` = the deferred scope has since
landed (by a later ledger row, a promotion, or current code) and has been
verified by an M0119 triage/consumption task. M0119 sets these values; appending
a new deferral row uses `-`.

| resolved | 2026-06-22 | M0118-0004 multixact-no-deadlock (deadlock-detection slice) — **multixact-no-deadlock PROMOTED to pass** | LANDED a pure-promotion (NO new engine code) of `multixact-no-deadlock` (TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoDeadlock byte-identical vs PG 18.3). Spec: s1 FOR SHARE; s2 FOR SHARE (row xmax becomes a SHARE multixact {s1,s2}); s3 FOR UPDATE WAITS behind the SHARE multixact; then s1 re-requests FOR SHARE (s1lock2) — a lock it already holds — and must NOT queue behind the waiting s3 (that would deadlock: s3 waits for s1's SHARE, s1 waits behind s3). PG returns s1lock2 immediately and only after s2+s1 COMMIT does s3 complete. FINDING: goopg's existing tuple-lock path already holds the invariant. In stampLockInner the wait/NOWAIT/SKIP branch is gated on tupleLockConflicts FIRST — re-FOR SHARE vs a SHARE multixact does not conflict so the branch is skipped entirely and s1 falls through to re-stamp. Even where a conflict exists activeLockHolders filters the current backend out of the wait set (m.Xid != Tx.XID) and stampMultiLock drops+re-appends self when re-forming the multixact; multixact.MembersConflict (port of DoesMultiXactIdConflict) skips self (m.Xid == reqXid). s3's FOR UPDATE is parked OUTSIDE the tuple's xmax (a waiter not yet stamped) so s1 sees only the compatible {s1,s2} members and has nothing to wait on — the heavyweight-lock deadlock detector is never consulted. The sibling EPQ walk epqFollowChainFull already handled this with a broader atTail test; the row-lock path had drifted. FIX: extracted isChainTailCTID(ctid, curBlk, curSlot) = (Block==InvalidBlockNumber \|\| Offset==0 \|\| self) and used it in BOTH epqFollowChainFull and stampLockInner (sibling-paths rule); the deleted-row return now signals epqSkipped=true so drainAndStamp DROPS the row → s2 sees (0 rows) instead of yielding the stale pre-delete version (matches PG EvalPlanQual returning no tuple). Both helpers are strict no-ops outside a savepoint (EffectiveWriterXID()==top-level; TopLevelXid(x)==x) so the 8 passing perms and every other isolation spec are unaffected. (2) Latent SubxactMap split fixed in internal/mvcc/manager.go: AllocateSubXid registered the sub-XID via addSubxactEntry (in-memory fallback map ONLY) while TopLevelXid/IsAborted/MarkSubxactAborted prefer the ATTACHED persistent SubxactMap (installed by initdb.Open SetSubxactMap = the real-server path); so on the real server TopLevelXid(subxid) returned the subxid unchanged and xidActiveWithSubxact took its top==xid early-false branch -&gt; the savepoint lock looked dead and conflictingLockHolders filtered it out (this is why fix 1 alone left s2 not blocking at step 8). FIX: AllocateSubXid now registers through RegisterSubXid which writes the attached map when present (best-effort pg_subtrans SLRU parent-link mirror like the lazy first-write path) and falls back to the in-memory map otherwise. Gaps A/B/C never hit this because pre-fix-1 lock members were stamped under the top-level xid which resolves via the xidInProgress fast path and never consults the subxact map. (2) an inheritance-child SeqScan now carries SkipIfVanished (planner inheritance branch); seqScanOp.Open, AFTER acquiring the child's scan lock (where the wait completes), returns zero rows if the child OID is no longer in the catalog (LookupTableByOID→!exists) — else NBlocks would O_CREATE-recreate the dropped relfile; a directly-scanned table still errors "does not exist". Result: s2sel plans {p,c1}, blocks on the lock, skips the vanished c1 → 1; 2nd s2sel re-plans {p} (or reuses {p,c1} whose c1 skips) → 1. Known limitation (DROP INDEX precedent): the deferred drop is invisible to the dropping session too until commit (shared catalog, no per-session MVCC); the spec never exercises it. A transactional-correctness subtlety the event-trigger precedent didn't have to face: `DROP FUNCTION` has TWO removal paths (autocommit-immediate via `execDropFunction`'s `else` branch, and deferred-to-COMMIT via `ApplyDeferredRoutineDrops` for an explicit-transaction drop, per M0118-0009 `stats`) plus CASCADE-dependent drops (`functionsDependingOnRoutineOID`, dropped immediately regardless of transaction state, no rollback-undo). All three are WAL-logged at the point the removal is actually durable/unconditional — the autocommit branch and CASCADE block log immediately (no rollback-undo tracking exists for either, so immediate logging can't diverge from a later ROLLBACK), while the deferred branch logs *inside* `ApplyDeferredRoutineDrops` itself (which only ever runs at real COMMIT — `operators_tx.go execCommit` and `dispatch.go`'s simple-query `TxCommit` case — never at ROLLBACK, which discards the deferred entries via `TakeDeferredRoutineDrops` without calling it), making the log point inherently rollback-safe rather than a copy-paste of the event-trigger "log at statement time" convention. Verified via a real `goopg stop`/`start` restart cycle against the same data dir (not just unit tests): `CREATE FUNCTION` (with a DEFAULT arg and numeric(10,2) typmod) + `CREATE FUNCTION IMMUTABLE` + `CREATE PROCEDURE` + a `DROP FUNCTION` all survive one restart; the dropped function and the pre-rename old name are correctly absent; `ALTER FUNCTION RENAME TO` + `ALTER FUNCTION STRICT SECURITY DEFINER` survive with the renamed name and all four flags intact; `CALL` on the restored procedure and a call on the restored function both still execute correctly against the recovered `Body`. Deferred rather than shipped-unsafely. SET` follow-up). Real PG's `set_rest` grammar production (`postgres/src/backend/parser/gram.y` ~line 1708) accepts six special syntaxes as alternatives to the generic `name TO|= value` form — `TIME ZONE zone_value`, `SCHEMA Sconst`, `NAMES opt_encoding`, `ROLE NonReservedWord_or_Sconst`, `SESSION AUTHORIZATION {NonReservedWord_or_Sconst|DEFAULT}`, `XML OPTION {DOCUMENT|CONTENT}` — each translating to a plain GUC name/value pair (`timezone`/`search_path`/`client_encoding`/`role`/`session_authorization`/`xmloption`); `SetResetClause` (shared by plain `SET` and `AlterDatabaseSetStmt`/`AlterRoleSetStmt`) reduces to the identical `set_rest` production, so all six are valid inside `ALTER DATABASE`/`ALTER ROLE ... New shared helper `parseSetRestSpecialForm` (`internal/server/database_ddl.go`) recognizes the six forms on the raw text following `SET ` and returns the translated `(configName, configValue, reset)` before the generic parse runs; called from both `parseAlterDatabaseConfig` and `parseAlterRoleConfig`. `TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT` deliberately excluded — its `VAR_SET_MULTI` kind has no case in `ExtractSetVariableArgs`, so real PG cannot store it via `AlterSetting` either (a transaction-scoped command, not a persistable GUC). Gates: `go build ./...` clean; `internal/server` suite PASS (full package, no regression); live `psql`/`pg_dumpall` smoke as described; `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33); pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook. | `SET ... FROM CURRENT` (reads the session's *current* GUC value rather than a literal — needs the session's live GUC lookup threaded through, which the six forms above did not need) remains unrecognised by both parse functions and falls through to no-op absorption, same as before this loop. | resolved | 2026-07-03 | M0119-0005 | Closes the loop #88/loop-#90-row-418 "unaudited: does the same HOT-class canonical-FPI gap exist at `markHeapPruneOptDirty`" flag — this loop confirms it does, and traces the SAME gap to the real VACUUM path too (a strictly bigger blast radius than the flag anticipated). Traced both pruning call sites: (1) opportunistic prune, `tryApplyHOTUpdate`'s page-full fallback (`internal/executor/operators_storage.go` ~3225-3234) calls `markHeapPruneOptDirty` (~2714), which only ever calls `pool.LogHeapPruneOpt()` — goopg's *native* `RecordKindHeapPruneOpt` (`internal/wal/recovery.go:105`) — with no `ctx.LogCanonical` sibling call anywhere in the function; (2) the real `VACUUM`/autovacuum path (`internal/executor/operators_vacuum.go`'s `vacuumOp.Next` → `vacuum.VacuumWithOptions`, `internal/vacuum/vacuum.go:56`) reclaims dead tuples via `storage.PageVacuumPrune` and logs ONLY `pool.LogHeapPruneOpt()`/`MarkDirtyChangeRecord` (`vacuum.go` ~107-183) — the `internal/vacuum` package has no `LogCanonical`-shaped parameter at all, so a plain `VACUUM tbl;` (the single most common real-world trigger of page pruning) emits zero PG-canonical WAL records for any page it prunes, regardless of the WAL writer's PageHeaders/PG-compat mode. Ruled out the generic `maybeEmitFPI`/`logFPI` hook (`internal/storage/bufpool.go:1182`, wired from `MarkDirty`/`MarkDirtyChangeRecord`) as a fallback safety net: it also only emits goopg's native `RecordKindPageImage` (`internal/wal/recovery.go:20`, via `wal.EncodePageImage`, `internal/initdb/open.go:379`) — a different native record kind, still not a PG rmgr-decodable payload. So a page whose ONLY WAL activity since the last canonical touch is pruning/VACUUM is invisible to `pg_waldump` in every mode (not just `--save-fullpage`), and would desync a real PG18 standby attached via `ctx.LogCanonical` (line-pointer/redirect state drifts from the primary, though live tuple *data* is unaffected — see caveat below). Not a blocker for any currently `pass_required` test: `TestPort_PgWaldump002SaveFullpage` (WD-003, the row directly above) exercises CTAS+HOT-UPDATE only, no VACUUM; `001_basic.pl`'s still-deferred server tier is about hash/gin/gist/spgist/brin AM filtering, unrelated. No code changed this loop — pure investigation, confirming and narrowing the prior flag rather than attempting the fix (see why). | A `catalog.PgCanonicalHeapPrune`-shaped canonical record (mirroring `PgCanonicalHeapInplace`'s single-full-page-image approach, `internal/catalog/canonical.go:121` — a standby restoring the whole page from the FPI needs no per-redirect/per-dead-slot detail, matching how `PgCanonicalHeapInplace`/`PgCanonicalHeapDelete` already simplify away real PG's `xl_heap_prune`/`xl_heap_vacuum` structs) wired into BOTH `markHeapPruneOptDirty` (needs a `ctx`/`LogCanonical` parameter it doesn't currently take — it's called with just `pool`) and `vacuum.VacuumWithOptions` (needs a new optional callback field on `VacuumOptions`, `internal/vacuum/vacuum.go:35`, threaded from `operators_vacuum.go`'s `vacuumOp.Next` ~line 130, which already holds `o.ctx.LogCanonical`). Suggested rmgr/info: real PG's `RM_HEAP2_ID` (9, distinct from this codebase's existing `canonicalRmgrHeap = 10`) with an `XLOG_HEAP2_PRUNE`-equivalent info byte — add both as new constants next to `canonicalRmgrHeap`/`canonicalInfoHeapInplace` (`canonical.go` ~23-32). Needs: a `PgCanonicalHeapPrune(rel, blk, page, xid, logFn)` function + unit test (mirror `TestPgCanonicalHeapInsert_NilLogFn`-style coverage in `canonical_test.go`), the two call-site wirings above, a regression test exercising `pg_waldump --rmgr=Heap2` (or equivalent) after an explicit `VACUUM` on a table with a dead tuple, and a design-doc update to `docs/design/0110-0002-pg-waldump-tap-port.md`. Also worth checking whether the opportunistic prune path inside `pruneTouchedTempPages` (`internal/executor/operators_indexonly.go:285`, temp-table-only) needs the same treatment, or whether temp relations are out of scope for standby/pg_waldump parity by definition (they are backend-private and never replicated in real PG, so likely N/A — confirm before wiring). | Genuinely a new-capability addition (new canonical record type + a public API signature change on `vacuum.VacuumWithOptions`/`VacuumOptions` touching every caller + two call-site wirings + tests + design doc), not a "quick audit" — the prior loop's flag underestimated the blast radius (it only knew about the opportunistic path; the real-VACUUM path turned out to have the identical gap and is architecturally the more important one, since VACUUM is the common real-world trigger). Exceeds a single "ONE task per loop" implementation pass; this loop scoped to confirming and fully specifying the gap so a future loop can implement it directly from this row without re-deriving the investigation. |
